id-0fVq.title: Bridges: green paint on the sides
id-0fVq.summary: Green paint is often on the sides of bridges in South and Central Kalimantan.

id-0rmy.title: Signs: churches and Christian signs
id-0rmy.summary: The country is mostly Muslim, so churches and other Christian signs point to the regions where Christians live.

id-2YZ4.title: Landscape: savannah, white car in Gen 3
id-2YZ4.summary: A savannah landscape occasionally seen on north Sumba. In Gen 3 you always see a white car.

id-2dyw.title: Roofs: plain sheet metal in the north
id-2dyw.summary: Plain sheet metal roofs are more common towards the north, where tiled roofs are not found, mostly on Kalimantan, Sulawesi and Sumatra.

id-32xY.title: Google car: black Gen 3 car
id-32xY.summary: Black Gen 3 coverage can be found almost everywhere, but is most common in Sulawesi.

id-3RMB.title: Google car: black cab, men sitting in the bed
id-3RMB.summary: A black cab with men sitting in the back of the truck can be seen near Jagasatru on Bali.

id-4NsT.title: Roofs: symmetrical triangle with two slopes
id-4NsT.summary: Sheet metal roofs with a symmetrical triangle shape and two levels of slope are mostly on Sulawesi, but appear elsewhere too.

id-5XRu.title: Pole: horizontal text painted on the pole
id-5XRu.summary: Pole paint with horizontal text is a good clue for Bali. It is usually dark blue, but can be light blue or green.

id-69xY.title: Satellite dishes: tilt shows equator side
id-69xY.summary: A dish pointing north means you are probably south of the equator, and the other way round. Dishes aim near the middle of West Kalimantan, so the angle shows which side of the country you are on and how far from the equator.

id-78MF.title: Currency: Rupiah (Rp)
id-78MF.summary: Prices on signs use Rp, the Rupiah.

id-8gpa.title: Google car: Gen 3 with antenna, main island
id-8gpa.summary: Gen 3 coverage with an antenna is most common on Java, especially East Java, and very rare near Denpasar on Bali. In the west it has been replaced by Gen 4.

id-8rxH.title: Google car: white SUV with black bars
id-8rxH.summary: A white SUV with black bars and a wooden plank on the roof is rarely seen in eastern Bali.

id-C0wR.title: Fences: painted white with blue or red
id-C0wR.summary: Painted fences, mostly white with blue or red, are typical for Sulawesi.

id-E9E9.title: Pole: even or uneven top bar
id-E9E9.summary: Poles have either an even (symmetrical) or an uneven bar holding the insulators. Learning where each type is common helps with region guessing.

id-EKlp.title: Pole: extra attachment under the top bar
id-EKlp.summary: In North and Central Sulawesi and Gorontalo, pole tops often have an extra attachment right under the horizontal bar.

id-H5BA.title: Pole: triangle under the horizontal bar
id-H5BA.summary: Some poles have a triangle attachment under the horizontal bar in certain regions. This does not apply to stacked poles.

id-H5zf.title: Roofs: steep palm-leaf roofs
id-H5zf.summary: Steeply pitched roofs made of palm leaves are sometimes seen on Nias Island, southwest of North Sumatra.

id-Hl5V.title: Pole: thin black pole, blue-green tape
id-Hl5V.summary: Thin black poles beside regular ones, with two pieces of tape near the top, usually light blue and green, in the east of Central Sulawesi. Rarely in northern South East Sulawesi.

id-HlrS.title: Sign: five-digit postal code
id-HlrS.summary: Some signs show a five-digit postal code. The first digit grows from 1 in the capital to 9 in the far east.

id-HsTd.title: Pole: A-shaped support
id-HsTd.summary: Poles with an A-shaped support are common in Kalimantan and the islands east of Java. A-frames can appear anywhere wires bend, so use with care.

id-K7j1.title: Fields: rice mostly on the main island
id-K7j1.summary: Most rice is grown on Java, though some is in South Sulawesi and South Sumatra, and rarely elsewhere.

id-L4lX.title: Banners: rows of red and white flags
id-L4lX.summary: Rows of red and white banners appear all over the country. More colourful flags sometimes appear too.

id-Lrxl.title: Roofs: boat-shaped, flatter, no spires
id-Lrxl.summary: North Sumatra has boat-shaped roofs too, but less angled upward and without spires, mostly near Lake Toba.

id-M7aC.title: Plate: black with three white sections
id-M7aC.summary: Plates are black with white letters, which look like three white blocks through the blur. Commercial vehicles have yellow plates, and newer coverage can show white ones. Malaysia's black plates usually show two blocks.

differs.how: Black plates usually show two white sections

id-MAU0.title: Ads: cigarette ads in black or red
id-MAU0.summary: Cigarette ads are everywhere, usually black or red with a price around 18,000 Rp. Look for the graphic warning pictures and the word PERINGATAN.

id-NAMC.title: Plate: motorcycles have front plates
id-NAMC.summary: Motorcycles carry a front licence plate, unlike other South-East Asian countries.

id-PPGB.title: Pole: trident-shaped top
id-PPGB.summary: Trident-style pole tops are most common in Central Java and Yogyakarta, and rare in southern and western Kalimantan, North Sumatra and Riau.

id-QclR.title: Language: compass words in addresses
id-QclR.summary: Addresses often have compass words: Utara north, Timur east, Selatan south, Barat west, Tengah central and Tenggara southeast.

id-SYxy.title: Language: Dutch-style spelling like "televisi"
id-SYxy.summary: Indonesian looks like Malay, but is influenced by Dutch, not English. For example "televisi" (like Dutch "televisie") against Malay "televisyen".

id-Sl44.title: Waystone: yellow, angled, cutout at top
id-Sl44.summary: Yellow waystones angled toward the road with a cutout near the top, showing short names of three towns with the biggest on top. In the Philippines waystones stand square to the road, facing away.

differs.how: Waystones stand square to the road, text facing away

id-UJod.title: Houses: raised, saddle-shaped roofs
id-UJod.summary: A small area of South Sulawesi around Rante Pao has Tongkonan houses with saddle-shaped roofs, lifted off the ground.

id-Ue6l.title: Coverage: limited, none in the far east
id-Ue6l.summary: Coverage is fairly limited. There is none in Papua or the nearby islands, and little in Kalimantan, Aceh, Central Sulawesi and North Maluku.

id-VrBB.title: Landscape: karst formations
id-VrBB.summary: Eastern South Kalimantan has karst rock formations, especially along the highway into East Kalimantan. Similar ones are in South Sulawesi and West Sumatra.

id-W7JT.title: Bollard: black bottom, white middle, yellow top
id-W7JT.summary: Bollards painted black at the bottom, white in the middle and yellow at the top are unique to Central Sulawesi.

id-WGZd.title: Sign: kabupaten (regency) names
id-WGZd.summary: Signs and billboards often show the second-level region, called Kabupaten or Kab (regency). 417 are covered, and with time they are learnable.

id-YrUA.title: Pole: even bar, uneven insulators
id-YrUA.summary: An even bar with one insulator on one side and two on the other is almost only found in North Sumatra.

id-YwXJ.title: Driving side: left
id-YwXJ.summary: Cars drive on the left. Malaysia also drives on the left, but the Philippines drives on the right.

id-a0Zq.title: Roofs: horizontal slots in the triangles
id-a0Zq.summary: Horizontal slots inside the triangles of roofs are almost unique to southern Sulawesi, rarely in East Kalimantan and West Nusa.

id-b5h6.title: Landscape: drier, low shrubby look
id-b5h6.summary: The islands east of Java are drier, with lower, shrubbier, browner vegetation, getting drier towards the east. Sumba is driest. Java can look this dry too.

id-bXHT.title: Camera: moiré-like glitch
id-bXHT.summary: A camera glitch that looks like a moiré pattern, seen throughout Central Kalimantan.

id-bas1.title: Roofs: made of wooden chips
id-bas1.summary: Unique roofs made of wooden chips are found on Kalimantan.

id-cPPJ.title: Pole: round steel or concrete
id-cPPJ.summary: Poles are round, steel or concrete. Many steel ones are painted black with the national flag colours. Pole tops are either even or uneven, depending on the region.

id-dZoK.title: Roofs: boat-shaped with spires
id-dZoK.summary: Distinct boat-shaped roofs are found in West Sumatra.

id-dZp8.title: Pole: indent on both sides
id-dZp8.summary: Poles with an indent on both sides are found in West Java, the capital area and Banten.

id-dxow.title: Plants: oil palm plantations
id-dxow.summary: Oil palm plantations are mostly in Sumatra and Kalimantan, and rarely in Sulawesi.

id-hOwL.title: Road lines: white or yellow centre, white edges
id-hOwL.summary: Centre lines can be white or yellow, solid or dashed, and edge lines are always white. Yellow is rarer in Gen 3 coverage. Malaysia's lines are always all white.

id-hYSj.title: Pole: extra long support on top
id-hYSj.summary: On the islands east of Java, poles often have an extra long support on top, sometimes two.

id-hewR.title: Pole: uneven top with two supports below
id-hewR.summary: Uneven poles with two supports below the bar are mostly on Sumatra and southern Sulawesi, not Kalimantan or Java.

id-hhbb.title: Landscape: lake with island, mountains
id-hhbb.summary: Mountains surround a lake with an island in the middle. Overcast coverage is common. This is the Lake Toba area.

id-iDjC.title: Roofs: gable horns
id-iDjC.summary: Horns on the roof gables are most common in South Sulawesi, Riau and Central and South Kalimantan. They often go with Bugis roofs in South Sulawesi.

id-l5TB.title: Landscape: round green hills, palms or corn
id-l5TB.summary: Very rounded green hills, covered in palms, sugarcane or corn, are extremely common in Gorontalo province.

id-lm-15390.title: Soil: red soil on small islands east of Sumatra
id-lm-15390.summary: Red soil is often found on Batam and the Bangka Belitung islands, east of mainland Sumatra.

id-lm-56020.title: Plants: red-tinged leaves everywhere, rock piles
id-lm-56020.summary: A plant with red-tinted leaves mixed in with green is everywhere on Nias and pretty much unique there. The island has North Sumatra poles, often metal, and random rock piles by the road.

id-lm-56021.title: Vegetation: many oil palms, flat, grid roads
id-lm-56021.summary: Many oil palms, very flat land and often straight roads in a grid, plus the North Sumatra pole.

id-lm-56022.title: Landscape: mixed crops, north-south grid
id-lm-56022.summary: Around the big city in North Sumatra, you often see corn and sugarcane as well as oil palms, rarely rice, and streets in a north-south grid.

id-lm-56025.title: Landscape: very distinct volcano, greenhouses
id-lm-56025.summary: A very distinct volcano is visible from far away around Berastagi. On the plateau the crops and farming gear differ, with greenhouses and very small fields.

id-lm-56026.title: Landscape: cleared grassy hills, planted trees
id-lm-56026.summary: Hills cleared of trees and very green, with grass only. Any trees look replanted and stand alone. Hills with nothing but grass mean a lake area. Mostly a feeling.

id-lm-56027.title: Houses: plain concrete blocks in rows
id-lm-56027.summary: Blocky concrete buildings with nothing decorative on the side, often above a garage and in rows next to each other. A good clue for North Sumatra and sometimes Riau.

id-lm-56028.title: Vegetation: oil palms point to one province
id-lm-56028.summary: Oil palms mean Riau, which has a lot of them.

id-lm-56029.title: Roofs: one specific gable horn
id-lm-56029.summary: This specific gable horn shape is unique to Riau.

id-lm-56030.title: Palms: areca palms in the west
id-lm-56030.summary: Areca palms (called Sumatra palms locally) are mostly on Sumatra, most often in the west of North Sumatra and the west coast. The west coast is hilly, the east coast flat.

id-lm-56031.title: Pipes: oil pipes toward the port
id-lm-56031.summary: Lots of oil palms in Riau, and the palm oil goes through pipes to the port of Dumai. Pipes mean you are near Dumai.

id-lm-56032.title: Soil: orange, almost yellowish
id-lm-56032.summary: Kundur Island has orange, almost yellowish soil.

id-lm-56033.title: Roofs: curved roof edges from the neighbour
id-lm-56033.summary: Malaysia has curves at the edges of roofs, which are not Indonesian in origin. So they are only found next to Malaysia: the east coast of Sumatra, the islands and West Kalimantan.

id-lm-56034.title: Vibe: feels like Singapore but isn't
id-lm-56034.summary: If it feels like Singapore but is not Singapore, it is probably Batam.

id-lm-56035.title: Soil: red soil, like an off-brand Singapore
id-lm-56035.summary: Batam has red soil. Think of it as an off-brand Singapore.

id-lm-56036.title: Buildings: big blocks standing alone
id-lm-56036.summary: Bintan is being prepared to be built up like Batam, so you see big buildings with no others around them, out of place, and lots of emptiness.

id-lm-56037.title: Roads: very well paved, lines on small roads
id-lm-56037.summary: In the richest part of Sumatra, roads are well paved and often have road lines even on small roads where you would not expect them.

id-lm-56038.title: Pole: symmetrical, supports at 35-40 degrees
id-lm-56038.summary: A symmetrical, often metal pole with connecting bars that go in at about 35 to 40 degrees from the middle of the crossbar to small connecting bits, not to the pole itself and not at 45 degrees.

id-lm-56040.title: Fields: rice is rare on this big island
id-lm-56040.summary: Within Sumatra, basically the only place you see rice is West Sumatra.

id-lm-56041.title: Land: mixed plantations beside wild land
id-lm-56041.summary: South Sumatra has poorly managed land, so you often see different plantations on each side of the road, or a plantation on one side and wild land on the other.

id-lm-56042.title: Houses: tiled roof, wooden front
id-lm-56042.summary: Often tiled roofs, with a wooden front, and the house raised off the ground. Once you see it you won't unsee it.

id-lm-56043.title: Trees: lots of rubber trees
id-lm-56043.summary: Lots of rubber trees in South Sumatra. They also appear in North Sumatra, but other clues tell them apart.

id-lm-56044.title: Roads: straight grid, not always north-south
id-lm-56044.summary: Most of Lampung is laid out in a grid with many straight roads, not always north-south.

id-lm-56045.title: Houses: spread out, modern, small porch columns
id-lm-56045.summary: Houses stand on their own, very spread out, in flat land. They feel more modern, often with columns holding up a small porch and tiled roofs.

id-lm-56046.title: Roadside: sticks along the road
id-lm-56046.summary: These sticks beside the road are Lampung about 80% of the time. Check other clues, as Sulawesi can have them too.

id-lm-56047.title: Roofs: tiles only along the creases
id-lm-56047.summary: Tiles only on the creases of roofs. This can occur elsewhere, but if all roofs are like that it is probably Bangka Belitung.

id-lm-56048.title: Roofs: very bright tiles mixed with normal ones
id-lm-56048.summary: Very bright tiles mixed in with normal coloured ones, not seen in Java. The share of tiled roofs fades from Lampung to Jambi.

id-lm-56050.title: Pole: oval with KJ and blue writing
id-lm-56050.summary: In Riau, an oval saying KJ with blue writing around it appears on poles.

id-lm-56290.title: Vibe: North Sumatra look with uneven poles
id-lm-56290.summary: Looks like North Sumatra (roofs, oil palms), but with uneven poles. Very limited coverage. This is Aceh.

id-lm-641021.title: Camera: purple tint and black blur
id-lm-641021.summary: Some Gen 4 coverage in Batam has a purple tint and a black blurred object, a camera glitch. It can also appear near Medan, so check other clues.

id-lm-641026.title: Pavement: brick paving
id-lm-641026.summary: Pavement made of bricks like this is found in East Java, especially around Surabaya.

id-lm-66451.title: Houses: white brick buildings on a dry island
id-lm-66451.summary: White brick buildings are a good clue for Timor, a very dry island in the far east.

id-lm-66453.title: Pole: central insulator on a side bracket
id-lm-66453.summary: Can be a trident pole but does not have to be. The way the central insulator is fixed to the side of the pole with an extra piece is what makes it unique to Central Java.

id-lm-66454.title: Pole: uneven, pole continues far above crossbar
id-lm-66454.summary: An uneven pole where the pole continues much higher than the crossbar. Within Java it most likely means East Java.

id-lm-66456.title: Pavement: central type
id-lm-66456.summary: This pavement style is about 80% accurate for Central Java within Java.

id-lm-66458.title: Walls: volcanic rock walls, dark fields
id-lm-66458.summary: In Java, rock walls that look volcanic, with dark fields and rocks by the road, mean you are probably in a volcanic area.

id-lm-66459.title: Pavement: square paving
id-lm-66459.summary: Square paving is not exclusive, but most common on Bali.

id-lm-66461.title: Shrines: Hindu shrines
id-lm-66461.summary: Hindu shrines are quite common on Bali.

id-lm-66462.title: Roofs: odd thatched-looking roofs
id-lm-66462.summary: Thatched-looking roofs are very common on Bali, sometimes in rice fields or by the road, and need not cover a whole house.

id-lm-66463.title: Pole: dark blue sticker
id-lm-66463.summary: A dark blue sticker on a pole is only found on Bali and Nusa Penida. A lighter version may be in the west Nusas and Lombok. Both fade.

id-lm-66464.hide: no learnable content (author does not know what the item is)

id-lm-66465.title: Language: unique local script
id-lm-66465.summary: A unique script from the island appears on signs.

id-lm-66466.title: Walls: grey brick or orange brick
id-lm-66466.summary: Two wall types, grey brick or orange brick, are not exclusive but quite common on Bali.

id-lm-66467.title: Roofs: tiled, crown on top, corner ornaments
id-lm-66467.summary: Tiled roofs, often with a crown and ornaments on the corners.

id-lm-66468.title: Bridge: gold and black with pedestals
id-lm-66468.summary: A typical bridge is gold and black with little statue pedestals at the ends. The statue itself need not be there, only the pedestal.

id-lm-66469.title: Landscape: like the main island but drier
id-lm-66469.summary: Has everything the main island has, but drier and with its own feel. Click around to get a feel.

id-lm-66470.title: Roofs: very dark grey tiles
id-lm-66470.summary: Roofs often have very dark, even grey, tiles. This is typical for Lombok.

id-lm-66471.title: Landscape: flat land between hills
id-lm-66471.summary: Most coverage is on flat land between hills or mountains you can see in the distance. In the east islands this means Sumbawa.

id-lm-66473.title: Huts: little shade huts in front of houses
id-lm-66473.summary: Small huts in front of houses give shade. They are found in the dry islands, often Lombok, and can be smaller than the one in the picture.

id-lm-66474.title: Landscape: flat means Lombok
id-lm-66474.summary: In the islands east of Java (except Sumba), if it is flat it is probably Lombok.

id-lm-66475.title: Landscape: mountains or tall hills
id-lm-66475.summary: In the islands east of Java, tall hills or mountains probably mean Flores.

id-lm-66476.title: Fences: painted fence on an eastern island
id-lm-66476.summary: The Sulawesi-style painted fence is common on the island of Sumbawa.

id-lm-66478.title: Plants: banana plants in the east
id-lm-66478.summary: If you think you are on Flores and see banana plants, you are probably in the east of it.

id-lm-66479.title: Landscape: extremely flat, dry savannah
id-lm-66479.summary: Only Sumba has this extremely flat, extremely dry savannah. In Gen 3, the car is white.

id-lm-66480.title: Landscape: low hills, not mountains
id-lm-66480.summary: In the islands east of Java, low hills (not taller mountains like Flores) point to mostly west or south Sumba.

id-lm-66482.title: Roofs: thatch-like, southeast
id-lm-66482.summary: These thatch-like roofs are exclusive to Timor, usually the southeast.

id-lm-66483.title: Palms: specific palm, local to one area
id-lm-66483.summary: If you see this palm you are probably in this general area.

id-lm-66484.title: Google car: very dry road, water to the north
id-lm-66484.summary: The most recognisable road in the country: Gen 3, really dry, with water to the north.

id-lm-68073.title: Fences: white with green tip
id-lm-68073.summary: A white fence with a green tip means you are probably on Peleng Island, and the coverage should show 2021 copyright.

id-lm-68074.title: Roads: grid layout like another province
id-lm-68074.summary: Southeast Sulawesi is often laid out in a grid, like Lampung, and can look like it at times.

id-lm-68075.title: Google car: white Gen 3, sunny, pines
id-lm-68075.summary: A white Gen 3 car, very sunny, sometimes with the local roof style, and often pines. Click around to get a feel.

id-lm-68076.title: Roofs: upward roof bottom completely straight
id-lm-68076.summary: Very similar to other roofs, but here the bottom edge going up is completely straight, not curved.

id-lm-68077.title: Houses: lots of blue
id-lm-68077.summary: Muna Island has a lot of blue, especially on houses.

id-lm-68078.title: Vibe: lots of blue, fairly dry
id-lm-68078.summary: Lots of blue and a fairly dry look. Click around to get the feel.

id-lm-68079.title: Landscape: green Iceland-like hills
id-lm-68079.summary: Green hills that look like Iceland point to around Mebula.

id-lm-68083.title: Landscape: valley with large mountains
id-lm-68083.summary: The city of Palu lies in a roughly north-south valley with large mountains on both sides.

id-lm-68084.title: Landscape: volcanoes
id-lm-68084.summary: North Sulawesi has a lot of volcanoes.

id-lm-68085.title: Roads: nice small roads
id-lm-68085.summary: North Sulawesi has nice small roads, like West Sumatra.

id-lm-68087.title: Roofs: porch roofs angled slightly down
id-lm-68087.summary: Roof extrusions at a slight downward angle are common in North Maluku.

id-lm-68088.title: Roofs: layered roofs
id-lm-68088.summary: Layered roofs are quite common in North Maluku.

id-lm-68089.title: Pole: even with supports at 45 degrees
id-lm-68089.summary: An even pole with the supports coming down directly to the pole at 45 degrees, found in North Maluku and West Kalimantan.

id-lm-68090.title: Houses: on a rock foundation off the ground
id-lm-68090.summary: Houses in North Maluku are often on a rock-like foundation a bit above the ground.

id-lm-68091.title: Landscape: rounded green hills with few trees
id-lm-68091.summary: Gorontalo has unique, roundish green rolling hills with few trees, some oil palms and often corn.

id-lm-68092.title: Roadside: rock piles and rock gutters
id-lm-68092.summary: North Maluku often has scattered piles of rock, and gutters and other items are sometimes made of rock.

id-lm-68093.title: Roofs: triangle with angled side flaps
id-lm-68093.summary: A roof with a triangle and flaps coming off the sides at a different angle is extremely common in South Sulawesi, often with gable horns. Unique ones have horizontal wood supporting the top triangle.

id-lm-68094.title: Coverage: 2021 copyright
id-lm-68094.summary: Peleng island coverage always shows 2021 copyright. This is not exclusive in its region but most common.

id-lm-709103.title: Plants: coconut palms
id-lm-709103.summary: Coconut palms are found in many regions but are most common along the coast, especially western Sumatra, southern Java, northern Sulawesi and North Maluku.

id-lm-709104.title: Plants: areca palms with short thick leaves
id-lm-709104.summary: Areca palms have fairly short, thick leaves and are most prominent in western Sumatra, with less common sightings elsewhere.

id-lm-709105.title: Trees: pines with long needles
id-lm-709105.summary: Sumatran pines grow in a few pockets, notably North Sumatra and Java. They have long needles, but she-oak has even longer ones.

id-lm-709106.title: Trees: coastal she-oak, long needle leaves
id-lm-709106.summary: Coastal she-oak grows along coasts in much of the country, especially Sumatra, Kalimantan and Java. Its leaves look like pine needles but are longer.

id-lm-709107.title: Palms: fan leaves, dense round crown, short
id-lm-709107.summary: Palmyra palms have fan-shaped leaves in a dense round crown and are usually short. They grow in dry parts: the islands east of Java and South Sulawesi.

id-lm-709108.title: Palms: fan leaves, open crown, taller
id-lm-709108.summary: Footstool palm has fan leaves like Palmyra, but the crown is more open, the leaves thinner and the palm taller. Mostly Sulawesi, rarely elsewhere.

id-lm-709109.title: Palms: very large stiff upright fan leaves
id-lm-709109.summary: Gebang palms have larger, stiffer, more upright leaves than the other fan palms. They flower once at the end of their life. Mainly Sulawesi and the islands east of Java.

id-lm-709110.title: Plants: cassava with hand-shaped leaves
id-lm-709110.summary: Cassava has small hand-shaped leaves, grown in plantations or half-wild near houses. Most common in Lampung and Java, with Lampung the hotspot.

id-lm-709111.title: Plants: giant milkweed with thick round leaves
id-lm-709111.summary: A small shrub with thick round leaves and pale flowers, found in dry regions: the islands east of Java and parts of Java and Sulawesi.

id-lm-709112.title: Plants: feathery leaves and pods
id-lm-709112.summary: White leadtree has delicate feathery leaves and often visible bean pods. It grows mainly on the dry islands east of Java and a few other dry areas.

id-lm-709114.title: Roofs: metal canopies with curved ends
id-lm-709114.summary: In the parts of Sumatra and Kalimantan facing Malaysia, many buildings have metal canopies with curved ends, often blue or red.

id-lm-78749.title: Google car: front of the car, mostly overwritten
id-lm-78749.summary: Most of this coverage is overwritten. You see the front of the car in the far north of North Kalimantan. If it is Gen 3, you probably shouldn't guess Kalimantan.

id-lm-78750.title: Landscape: piles of coal on a river
id-lm-78750.summary: Around the Mahakam River you often see piles of coal being exported.

id-lm-78751.title: Roads: cut through the forest
id-lm-78751.summary: Unlike Sumatra, most Kalimantan roads are cut through forest, with everything carved in on the roadside.

id-lm-78753.title: Soil: sometimes red dirt
id-lm-78753.summary: West Kalimantan sometimes has red dirt.

id-lm-78754.title: Pole: silver reflective wrap
id-lm-78754.summary: A silver reflective wrap around the pole is found in South Kalimantan and the major roads out of it.

id-lm-78755.title: Landscape: flat with one or two hills
id-lm-78755.summary: West Kalimantan is mostly flat apart from the occasional hill or mountain, so you often see flat land with one or two hills near you.

id-lm-78756.title: City: many canals and waterways
id-lm-78756.summary: Pontianak has many canals and waterways, a good clue for the west coast of Kalimantan.

id-lm-790726.title: Roof ornament: snake-dragon, raised head
id-lm-790726.summary: In Wajo Regency you sometimes see gable ornaments shaped like a snake-like dragon with a raised head.

id-lm-790727.title: Roof ornament: upward curl like a breaking wave
id-lm-790727.summary: A roof ornament with an upward curling shape like a breaking wave is exclusive to South Sulawesi, specifically Wajo Regency.

id-lm-790728.title: Gable horns: curved and elaborate
id-lm-790728.summary: Curved, very elaborate gable horns are mostly in North and East Kalimantan, which have the largest Dayak populations.

id-lm-790729.title: Gable horns: crossed rooster heads
id-lm-790729.summary: On Selayar Island, gable horns made of crossed rooster heads, sometimes with small figures of people.

id-lm-790730.title: Gable horns: two hooks pointing down
id-lm-790730.summary: In Jambi, gable horns are two hooks with downward-pointing ends.

id-lm-790731.title: Roof ornament: crossed bars along the ridge
id-lm-790731.summary: Crossed ornaments all along the roof ridge are found on Nias Island. Crossed bars also appear in Kalimantan on a chief's house with a rabbit-ear variant.

id-lm-790732.title: Roof ornament: vertical finials, rounded or flat
id-lm-790732.summary: Vertical finials are largely limited to West Sulawesi, in a rounded or a flat version.

id-lm-790733.title: Gable horns: X-shaped
id-lm-790733.summary: X-shaped horns are spread like winged gable horns, but can also be found in Jambi and the Riau Islands.

id-lm-790734.title: Gable horns: serrated lower edge
id-lm-790734.summary: Winged gable horns have a serrated lower edge. They are most common in South Sulawesi but also found across Sulawesi and eastern Kalimantan.

id-lm-790735.title: Gable horns: long ornate rabbit ears
id-lm-790735.summary: Long, ornate rabbit-ear gable horns are found in South Kalimantan.

id-lm-790736.title: Gable horns: ornate leafy tridents
id-lm-790736.summary: Ornate, leaf-patterned trident-shaped gable horns are found in South Kalimantan.

id-lm-790737.title: Gable horns: floral antler shapes
id-lm-790737.summary: Gable horns with rich floral patterns that look like antlers are found mostly in Riau and the Riau Islands, often with floral decorations on the gable too.

id-lm-790739.title: Roof ornament: buffalo horns
id-lm-790739.summary: Buffalo-horn roof ornaments are spread like winged gable horns but more common in South East and West Sulawesi.

id-lm-790740.title: Roof ornament: simple modern spear shape
id-lm-790740.summary: On Batam and Bintan you often see simple, modern spear-shaped roof ornaments, usually gold or yellow, rarely white, often with floral gable decorations.

id-lm-790741.title: Roof ornament: dagger between two curved horns
id-lm-790741.summary: On Rote Island, a roof ornament looks like a dagger between two upward-curving horns.

id-lm-790742.title: Roof ornament: three-part leafy design
id-lm-790742.summary: An intricate leafy ornament in three parts, one vertical and two along the roof sides, found in West Sulawesi and South Kalimantan.

id-p091.title: Soil: white soil on top of red
id-p091.summary: Red soil with a layer of white on top is most common on the Bangka Belitung islands, where the white often spills onto the road.

id-qYf4.title: Landscape: bay with mountains west, flat east
id-qYf4.summary: A bay facing slightly north-west with mountains to the west and a flat, built-up area to the east, just north of Palu.

id-r8SA.title: Houses: crown-like roof tips, carved stone
id-r8SA.summary: Crown-like roof pinnacles, guardian statues and slit-drum towers are common on Bali, plus carved gates and walls of dark volcanic andesite stone.

id-rHW9.title: Pole: rectangle attachment on the top
id-rHW9.summary: A rectangular attachment on pole tops is mostly unique to Bali, often with the extra long support seen on the nearby islands.

id-u0Sw.title: Bollard: black-white blocks or yellow-black
id-u0Sw.summary: Common bollards are black-and-white squares or circles, or yellow-and-black ones that may have a red reflector. UK-style bollards are mostly found on one big island.

id-xYgP.title: Roofs: very high-pitched peaks
id-xYgP.summary: Distinct roofs with unusually high peaks are found on the island of Sumba.

id-xaSG.title: Roofs: tiled
id-xaSG.summary: Tiled roofs are most common on Java, and sometimes in southern Sumatra, the islands east of Java and South Kalimantan. Tiles in South Kalimantan and Jambi look flatter and less rounded.

id-yzpd.title: Pole: crossbar flat side facing away
id-yzpd.summary: Poles with the flat part of the crossbar facing away from the pole are common in Sulawesi. Elsewhere it is attached to the pole.
